newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says close to trade agreement with Canada.
newsitem.headline: Chile says close to trade agreement with Canada.

text.p: Chile and Canada are close to signing a bilateral trade accord after negotiators thrashed out most outstanding issues in the latest round of talks in Ottawa, Chilean Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said Thursday.
"The treaty is currently around 90 percent completed," Aninat told reporters.
The Chilean delegation returned to Santiago on Wednesday after reaching agreement on most of the important sticking points, Aninat said in an interview with local television.
"There have been important advances. A series of issues have been dealt with favourably for the country (Chile) including the issue of the reserve requirement which was accepted," he said.
Canada had originally rejected Chilean rules forcing foreign investors to deposit the equivalent of 30 percent of their investment with the central bank for a year.
Disagreements over the reserve rules had delayed the treaty which had been expected to be signed by mid-October.
Aninat said the accord may be now completed within a month, which would mean it could be signed during President Eduardo Frei's visit to Canada Nov. 17-18.
Chile hopes the agreement will be a stepping stone towards membership of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) which groups Canada, the United States and Mexico.
"This is a second generation agreement which brings us closer to NAFTA," said Aninat.
Talks on Chile's much-vaunted entry to NAFTA stalled last year due to internal political difficulties in Washington.

The bilateral accord, which is designed to be compatible with the terms of NAFTA, sweeps away immediately tariffs on two thirds of the trade between the two countries. The remaining duties will be reduced over 18 years.
Canadian businessmen are the second largest foreign investors in Chile with billions of dollars invested mainly in the fast-growing mining industry.
